glosses: unbeabsichtigt oder unkontrolliert fieren

examples.text: Die Enden werden dann derart verschmolzen, dass sie eine Verdickung bilden, damit die Knoten nicht ausrauschen.
Wird nur eine Seite belastet, kann der Ankerstich ausrauschen oder – falls der Ring einen zu kleinen Radius hat – umkippen und sich so ungewollt lösen.
Wenn eine unter Last stehende Schot unkontrolliert ausrauscht, stellt dies eine erhebliche Gefahr für die Besatzung dar und das Schiff wird wegen des schlagenden Segels schwer steuerbar.
Die Crew am Spill löst die Bremse und lässt den Anker ausrauschen bis er den Grund erreicht hat.
Tipp: Mit dem Fallen des Ankers nicht zu viel Kette (Leine) ausrauschen lassen.

translations.source_sense_description: Seemannssprache, von Leinen oder Ankerketten: unbeabsichtigt oder unkontrolliert fieren

glosses: To release from one's grasp; to go from a state of holding on to a state of no longer holding on.

examples.text: You're hurting him! Let him go!
Let go of the phone.
He had one hand on the bounce bottle—and he'd never let go of that since he got back to the table—but he had a handkerchief in the other and was swabbing his deadlights with it.

But it wasn’t ransom enough.
His captors accepted it all,
But didn’t let go of the king.
Falling from cloud nine / Crashing from the high / I'm letting go tonight / Yeah, I'm falling from cloud nine

glosses: To emotionally disengage or distract oneself from a situation.

examples.text: You are supported, so you can just let go and relax. Inhale and slowly exhale.

glosses: To dismiss from employment.

examples.text: The secretary didn't work out, so her boss told her she was being let go.

Puel was let go in June despite leading Southampton to their first major final for 14 years and an eighth-place finish in the Premier League. But apparently his style was too boring and some players and many fans disliked his method, so he had to go – fair enough but look at them now.

glosses: To ignore (a comment, etc.).

examples.text: Cora gave her shoulders a rebellious toss. "I'm sick of always getting oysters; I'd sooner come out with you." Bradly let that go. "You had enough money this week without getting oysters, didn't you?"

glosses: To fail to maintain a standard of appearance, behavior, or performance.
To fail to maintain a standard of appearance, behavior, or performance.
To gain weight.

examples.text: Wow, dude! You've really let yourself go this time!

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see let, go.

examples.text: Please, Mom, can you let me go to her party?
We shan’t let our old car go to anyone for less than 15 grand.

glosses: Alternative spelling of runout.
To use up or consume all

examples.text: Get some more beer out of the fridge before we run out.
If this hot weather continues, we will run out of ice cream.

England keeper Joe Hart had to save smartly from the dangerous Andriy Yarmolenko, who also raised the hopes of the Donetsk crowd as he evaded several challenges in the area before running out of space.

glosses: To expire; to come to an end.

examples.text: My driving licence runs out next week, so I had better renew it now.
The option will run out next week and I can't get it extended.

glosses: To expire; to come to an end.
To be completely used up or consumed.

examples.text: Time is running out, so I renounce a spin on a Class 387 for a fast run to Paddington on another Class 800 - a shame as the weather was perfect for pictures. Even so, it's enjoyable - boy, can those trains shift under the wires.
Time is running out.
Oh no! The wine has run out!

Mario Balotelli replaced Tevez but his contribution was so negligible that he suffered the indignity of being substituted himself as time ran out, a development that encapsulated a wretched 90 minutes for City and boss Roberto Mancini.

glosses: To get a batsman out (dismissed from play) via a runout.

examples.text: Jackson was run out for a duck in the first over.
With three runs needed from two balls, Adil Rashid was run out coming back for a second. When Wood suffered the same fate from the final ball, the match was tied.

glosses: To extend a piece of material, or clothing.

examples.text: If I run out these curtains, they will fit the windows in the drawing room.

glosses: To conclude in, to end up.

examples.text: Tottenham survived a scare as they fought back from 1-0 down to run out comfortable winners against Shamrock Rovers in the Europa League.

glosses: To force (someone or something) out of a location or state of being.

examples.text: If the mob thinks you did it, they'll run you out of town.
They'll run us out of business doing that!

glosses: To grow poor over time by spending all of one's money.
To fill a line with quadrats or full points.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see run, out.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: see Thesaurus:leave
She ran out of the room in tears.
